approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from the current session’s accepted molecules. It draws ranked breeding parents, applies fragment crossover and ordinary graph mutations, checks canonical identities and source-relative sulfur admission, and builds a fresh offspring pool. A Gaussian process with count-Morgan similarity, fixed covariance settings and standardized raw scores guides purchases through correlated function draws. After three batches without an incumbent improvement it restricts eligibility to the forty largest predictive means; accepted raw scores update the archive, survivors and later breeders. The Parent has already removed an unexposed rejection-conditioned mutation floor, while retaining ordinary stochastic continuation.
approach.novelty: Learn one invertible output law from the current accepted scores and use that same law for both training and prediction. A positive linear term plus three monotone tanh terms is fitted by likelihood including its Jacobian. Inverse-transformed joint draws guide purchases, and the expectation of the inverse marginal supplies the existing mean-based eligibility rule. The earlier rank-transform sibling replaced cardinal spacing with fixed empirical normal ranks and lost paid ordering accuracy; this intervention retains cardinal information, fits a probabilistic transform and returns predictions to raw score units. It is one coupled output-law change, with no covariance or generator change.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior targeted here is the Parent’s inability to adapt the shape of its predictive output law: FingerprintPosterior.fit always uses affine-standardized raw labels with a fixed Gaussian likelihood, and distribution/select always consume a Gaussian raw-space law. This is a specific modeling constraint, not established proof that miscalibration causes the search plateau. The complete Parent n-cf8d309c06de has mean 0.607030316211131 and seed SD 0.030175277546149237. Reopening all fifteen Search logs and trajectories finds 4350 purchases, 435 successful fits, mean batch paid Spearman 0.5152643987768258, full positive generating-parent gain 16.891241376231875 and late gain 4.40236982945407 (optimizer ordinals 146..290). Its strong ordering and known proposal/scaffold limitations are contrary evidence against calling the predictor generally broken. The specific fixed-rank attempt n-8c806cf9b586 did activate yet decreased strict-pair accuracy from same-state raw-GP 0.6857290857290858 to 0.6677544677544678 and endpoint mean by 0.034871956463797704. The older-host n-ae12ccae8c7b likewise changed all 435 target fits but reduced same-paid-label mean Spearman from 0.48429892962973947 to 0.4431662971746234 and endpoint mean by 0.021067064526871015; its execution verdict remains confirmed even though those benefit predictions failed. These B1 results and the frozen B3 likelihood-warp review justify a different fitted-law test, not another rank recipe. Source audit: policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/source-audit.json; underlying policy/nodes/n-cf8d309c06de.json, policy/nodes/n-8c806cf9b586.json, policy/nodes/n-ae12ccae8c7b.json and their complete indexed Search summaries/run logs/task logs/trajectories.

adoptions.applicability: Only current-session accepted cardinal scores train this output map. Bounded repeated molecular scores, small adaptive samples and a fixed covariance limit transfer; the paper supplies a construction, not campaign efficacy.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Sections 3.1–3.3: monotone onto-real output transformation, Jacobian-adjusted likelihood, inverse predictive quantiles and Gauss-Hermite expectation distinct from the inverse-mean median.

deviations.adopted_setting: Learn d in [0.1,10] and three bounded tanh terms while fixing the inherited count kernel and noise.
deviations.paper_setting: A unit linear term accompanies monotone tanh terms; covariance parameters can be learned.
deviations.reason: The positive slope permits contraction without covariance fitting and preserves an onto-real inverse.

deviations.adopted_setting: One deterministic bounded optimizer, fresh near-identity initialization, fixed inverse tolerances and 128-point quadrature; actual paid-label prospective loss.
deviations.paper_setting: Likelihood fitting and inverse-density prediction in regression.
deviations.reason: These numerical and evaluation choices are campaign adaptations frozen before outcomes.

adoptions.implementation_change: FingerprintPosterior.fit minimizes the registered transformed likelihood; select maps the unchanged correlated latent draws through the fitted inverse and supplies its quadrature expectation to the existing mean consumer.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen planning review and its likelihood-warp source, checked against the primary paper. Internal evidence rejects another fixed-rank recipe but does not prove the Parent is miscalibrated. Test the learned output law once with cardinal likelihood and consistent raw prediction. No other reviewed portfolio method is adopted, no new model/package is introduced, and any advantage remains conditional on this adaptive finite Search panel.

sources.applicability: Adopt the probabilistic transform, not empirical ranks. Adapt to fixed count covariance and a learned positive linear slope, with deterministic fitting. Bounded repeated molecular targets and selected labels limit transfer; no paper score is campaign evidence.
sources.finding: A fitted monotone invertible output map enters the GP likelihood through its derivative; predictions return through its inverse. The paper uses tanh sums with a linear term and quadrature for predictive means.
sources.title: Warped Gaussian Processes

method_change.previous_method: Fixed affine-standardized raw-target Gaussian likelihood and Gaussian predictive consumer in n-cf8d309c06de.
method_change.proposed_method: Jacobian-fitted positive-linear/three-tanh invertible output likelihood with inverse joint draws and quadrature predictive mean.
method_change.rationale: The actual code Parent cannot learn output geometry; the two fixed empirical-rank attempts reduced paid ordering despite execution. A learned cardinal output likelihood is a distinct B1/B3-supported test with raw-space prospective predictive evaluation. Preserve the complete generator, count covariance, noise, randomness and real feedback state so the result identifies the joint output-law replacement.

hypothesis: Replace only the accepted-label output likelihood and its consistent predictive consumer within m-000000000005. With unchanged accepted raw mean m and population-SD/floor scale s, set t=(y-m)/s and g(t)=d*t+sum_{j=1}^3 a_j*tanh(b_j*(t+c_j)). Fit d in [0.1,10], a_j,b_j in [0,5], c_j in [-5,5] by minimizing 0.5*g(t)^T C^-1*g(t)+sum(log(diag(L)))+n/2*log(2*pi)-sum(log(g_prime(t)))+n*log(s), where C=LL^T is exactly the inherited fixed count-kernel training covariance including its original noise and realized jitter. No post-warp renormalization, rank target, new observation noise, covariance fit or regularizer is added. The positive linear coefficient makes the map strictly increasing and onto the real line and permits contraction despite fixed covariance. Condition on g(t); apply g^-1 to the original correlated latent function draws and restore m+s*inverse. Use the expectation of that same inverse marginal, approximated by fixed 128-point deterministic Gauss-Hermite quadrature, as the active raw predictive mean for the unchanged K=3/M=40 rule. The inverse of the latent mean is a median, not this mean. A common monotone inverse alone preserves a draw row’s candidate ordering; changed purchases must come from the fitted latent posterior and/or the consistent mean eligibility consumer, which jointly constitute this intervention.

finding_summary.headline: Nonlinear warping changed purchases, but one failed fit leaves the predictive test inconclusive and endpoints lower
finding_summary.insights: This separates an observable change in predictive geometry from a useful endpoint result. The available-prediction stream shows narrower tail errors and slightly better same-label ordering, while local parent-beating gains increase and total incumbent improvement decreases. Improving these intermediates therefore did not establish better search in this run. The source’s learned likelihood, inverse draws and expectation-based mean all operated on successful batches, but its transfer is limited by fixed covariance, the learned linear-slope adaptation, repeated bounded scores and the declared deterministic solver: one fit failed, 21 accepted fits were affine, and 432 of 435 attempted fits touched a bound. A different likelihood or estimation method would be needed to test robustness to these conditions; this result does not establish which one would improve endpoints. The chemistry report also shows that broader scaffold coverage can coexist with weaker endpoints and awkward heteroatom bonds or overgrown ring systems. A proposal operator that reorganizes scaffolds while preserving coherent local chemistry addresses a different observed limitation than output calibration. Neither improved observed-subset loss nor scaffold novelty proves mediation, and the failed complete-prediction conjunction leaves the learned-law approach open without overturning earlier fixed-rank findings.
finding_summary.results: The learned law changed actual search choices: 413 successful fits were nonlinear, and 410 of those batches bought a different set than the same-state raw Gaussian rule. One other fit hit the fixed 200-iteration limit and fell back to generation order, leaving ten purchases without prospective predictions. Thus the registered complete-panel predictive test is inconclusive. On the remaining 4,340 purchases, mean pinball loss was lower, 0.01702 versus 0.02000, and 90% interval coverage rose from 71.13% to 84.38%; neither figure substitutes for the missing full-panel measurement. All fifteen formal endpoints completed. Mean final best score fell from 0.60703 to 0.57217 (paired change −0.03486), with losses in every seed macro, so the required 0.60903 target was not reached. Full and late gains over generating parents nevertheless rose from 16.891/4.402 to 18.155/5.405.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles and amine-containing frameworks, with fragile heteroatom bonds, size extremes and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers n-80d9b7174bc7 against its published code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, under the frozen profile epoch 1, batch 10, Search seeds 0/1/2 and all five issued tasks. The request reports both child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with no profile-mismatched seeds. All 15 Child and 15 Parent trajectory files exist and contain 300 accepted evaluation records each, including the 10 supplied initial records; no task or seed comparison is absent. Per task, 870 Child optimizer rows are observed. These files describe accepted evaluated chemistry, not rejected proposals or the unpurchased offspring pool. No other node history is needed for the comparisons below. The output contains fused heteroaromatics, lactams and other cyclic carbonyl groups, substituted aryl amides, saturated nitrogen rings, ethers, fluorinated substituents and occasional very small fragments. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9609 to 1.0 and aromatic-atom presence rates from 0.8667 to 1.0; these are molecule-level text indicators, not aromatic atom fractions. Every task has zero explicit stereocentre and charged-text rates. Neutral SMILES nevertheless contain protonatable amines, and absence of @ does not mean absence of possible stereocentres. The molecules are not uniformly simple, acyclic or lacking basic ring nitrogen. Their weakness is uneven chemical coherence: complex fused and medium-sized rings coexist with N-halogen, O-halogen, peroxide, N-S or N-N motifs and highly elaborated side chains. These are structural concerns, not measured instability, synthesis failure or biological activity. Some normal amides, heterocycles and amines look plausible in isolation, but no route or stereochemical preparation is demonstrated. The scaffold repertoire is substantial while high-score series remain locally related; scaffold counts do not establish useful diversity or attribution to the output-law intervention. All reported descriptor counts are derived from the supplied trajectories using the documented RDKit procedure in policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/source-audit.json, with source hashes and complete per-seed examples. Small means <=5 heavy atoms and large means >50 heavy atoms only for these descriptive bins. Fragment-excluded similarity is maximum binary Morgan radius-2, 2048-bit Tanimoto to the same cell initial molecules after excluding <=5-heavy-atom molecules from both sets; it is a diagnostic, not a reward. Typed/generic scaffolds are Bemis-Murcko representations including the empty category. Exact source files are cited per task; this report makes no mechanism-activation, component-contribution, task-safety or selection decision.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted molecules are mostly compact polycyclic heteroaromatics carrying an aryl amide or cyclic carbonyl, methoxy/methyl substituents and often halogens. Median heavy-atom count is 25 (range 1-45), with median 4 rings and 3 aromatic rings. Seed-best structures have 23-24 heavy atoms: a fused nitrogen-rich aromatic aryl amide bearing N-S, a pyridyl-substituted fused lactam, and an indole amide fused to a chlorinated small carbocycle. They look recognizably medicinal in size, but the unusual fusion patterns and N-S linkage make synthesis uncertain. Parent median size was also 25 heavy atoms; typed/generic scaffold counts are 355/182 versus Parent 187/70, and fragment-excluded mean initial similarity is 0.298315 versus 0.339084. This is more scaffold variation in this panel, not evidence that every new framework is useful. Search sources (run-relative, Child copies are byte-identical to the frozen-request originals): policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl.
liabilities: The pooled best aryl amide has an N-S bond to terminal sulfur; this is a less conventional motif than an ordinary secondary or tertiary amide.
N-halogen and O-halogen SMARTS occur in 56 and 14 accepted optimizer molecules, respectively. These counts flag bond types, not proven synthetic failures.
Strained small fused rings and unspecified configurations complicate route plausibility; several late molecules add hydrazine-like or sulfur-containing edits without recovering the best score.
missing_features: Consistent retention of a compact, connected heteroaromatic/carbonyl framework is missing from the low-score tail: 34 accepted proposals contain <=5 heavy atoms.
Stereochemical specification is absent even when a saturated fused ring can introduce stereocentres; the visible scores do not establish a benefit from resolving them.
The evidence does not identify a unique missing target substructure beyond these within-panel associations; the best compounds already contain substantial ring and acceptor chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The Child seed-best scores are 0.4597940970593737, 0.458386638264238 and 0.4484138510190879; the corresponding Parent best scores were 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554. The leading Child molecules retain a substantial fused heteroaromatic framework and positioned carbonyl/amide functionality, while methane and fluorodisulfane score 0.0. Among the 87 highest-scoring accepted optimizer rows, median size is 24 heavy atoms and 4 rings, versus 9 heavy atoms and 1 ring in the 87 lowest. This supports a local association with compact, intact ring-and-carbonyl combinations; it does not establish that N-S chemistry or extra fusion is required. The final recorded molecule in seed 2 scores 0.33454192366627883, below that seed best, so terminal proposals are not equivalent to retained best chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted output is large and heavily ringed: median 40 heavy atoms, 5 rings and 5 aromatic rings, with a range of 1-74 heavy atoms. Seed-best structures contain 42, 42 and 44 heavy atoms. They include dense aza-aromatic fused systems with cyclic carbonyl groups, alkoxy and thioether substituents, and, in seed 2, an alkyne-containing ring system linked to a nitrogen heterocycle and multiple acyl/thioacyl groups. These are elaborate graph products whose individual functional groups are recognizable but whose full routes and ring closures are doubtful. Parent median size was 32 heavy atoms. Child typed/generic scaffold counts are 333/227 versus 347/241 for Parent; the larger size therefore does not correspond to more scaffold categories. Fragment-excluded mean initial similarity is 0.217579 versus 0.194746. Search sources (run-relative, Child copies are byte-identical to the frozen-request originals): policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl.
liabilities: There are 35 accepted proposals above 50 heavy atoms, compared with 18 in Parent, despite six Child fragment-sized proposals. Large size is neither uniformly rejected nor sufficient for a strong score.
O-halogen bonds occur in 123 Child molecules versus 55 Parent molecules. The cited seed-2 best and late products contain an aryl O-Cl group; this is an unusual reactive bond motif.

Multiple acyl/thioacyl groups, constrained alkynes, densely fused aza-aromatics and unspecified unsaturated side chains raise synthesis and stability questions that the numeric objective does not settle.
missing_features: The Child does not consistently combine a compact scaffold with the higher-scoring heterocycle/substituent arrangement seen in the Parent; the leading Child frameworks are substantially larger. The exact causal missing motif is not identifiable from these adaptive trajectories.
Route-plausible scaffold replacement with controlled ring closure and preserved useful substituent geometry is not demonstrated by the dense fused products.
Resolved stereochemistry and alkene geometry are not established for the elaborated products; no score benefit for imposing either can be inferred here.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The small fragments COF, CCOF and FCCF sit at 0.5, while the leading elaborated seed-1 series reaches 0.6309238428913886. Several distinct side-chain/fusion edits tie at that exact best score, so their individual substituents cannot be declared rewarded. Child seed-best scores are 0.6274509803921569, 0.6309238428913886 and 0.6117032178725148, versus Parent 0.8561477222467935, 0.6217289889933668 and 0.6442339647723496. Parent seed 0 reached its higher score with a smaller 30-heavy-atom fused nitrogen/carbonyl/thione framework. Thus the visible gradient favors substantial organized heterocyclic structures over tiny fragments, but the Child does not show that making the structures larger and more fused recovers the Parent high-score pattern. The 0.5 floor and repeated scores limit fine-grained inference.

per_task.generated_character: The high-score molecules clearly include basic nitrogen chemistry: aryl-substituted pyrrolidine/azetidine-like or other saturated nitrogen rings, secondary/tertiary amine linkers, and halogenated aromatic groups with phenol, methoxy or thiol substituents. Seed 2 also develops a bridged oxygen-containing ring system attached to a nitrogen-rich saturated ring. The full accepted stream is heavier than these leaders: median 35 heavy atoms and 9 rotatable bonds, versus Parent 29 heavy atoms and 7 rotatable bonds. Median ring count is 4 and aromatic ring count 2. Child typed/generic scaffolds are 443/272 versus Parent 327/202; fragment-excluded mean initial similarity is 0.274091 versus 0.205635. Synthetic plausibility is mixed: conventional amines and aryl rings coexist with awkward ring systems and fragile substituents. Search sources (run-relative, Child copies are byte-identical to the frozen-request originals): policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-0/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-1/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-2/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl.
liabilities: The seed-0 best contains an aryl hydroperoxide alongside sulfur-oxide and aminal-like functionality; its high score does not certify stability.
Child N-halogen/O-halogen counts are 132/218 versus Parent 35/76. Long flexible linkers, free thiol/aniline motifs and reactive heteroatom bonds remain among otherwise plausible-looking analogues.
The stream includes 20 molecules above 50 heavy atoms and 3 molecules with <=5 heavy atoms; the broad size tail is not reflected by the compact pooled best.
missing_features: Consistent production of the compact amine-bearing aryl arrangement is missing across the full stream; many lower-scoring compounds are larger and retain sulfonylated or acylated nitrogen instead.

Controlled configuration and conformational presentation are missing even in the high-scoring bridged and substituted saturated-ring products. The trajectories do not establish which stereoisomer, if any, is preferred.

There is no general absence of basic ring nitrogen to repair: it is already a prominent feature of the high-scoring molecules. Protonation states and actual affinity are not supplied by these neutral SMILES.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The Child seed-best scores are 0.9791044530062256, 0.9999888724879825 and 0.9870655468392702, versus Parent 0.980206046238846, 0.9999921067161532 and 0.9735180254338864. The pooled Child best is a 28-heavy-atom aryl pyrrolidine connected through a flexible carbon chain to an aminochlorophenyl group. Low-scoring examples include an N-chloro carboxamide on a sulfonylated nitrogen ring (0.00016650955053713697) and an acetyl analogue (0.00021169315013374197), which lack the leaders' extended amine-bearing aryl arrangement. The upper 87 optimizer rows have median 29 heavy atoms, 2 aromatic rings and carbon sp3 fraction 0.44; the lower 87 have medians 41, 3 and 0.2727272727272727. Within this panel, organized aromatic contacts plus saturated amine-bearing geometry accompany high scores, while excess size or simply having nitrogen does not. These are score associations, not a validated receptor-binding or pharmacological interpretation.

per_task.generated_character: This stream is entirely ring-bearing and aromatic by the digest counters. Typical molecules combine quinoline-like or larger fused aza-aromatic frameworks with ethoxy/propyl groups, lactam or diketone functionality and partially saturated nitrogen-containing rings. Median heavy-atom count is 32 (range 11-51), median rings 4 and median aromatic rings 2. The seed-1 best is a large fused aza-aromatic framework carrying a medium-sized nitrogen-containing ring with a ketone; the other seed leaders contain more clearly lactam/dicarbonyl-rich saturated ring systems. They are substantial, heteroatom-rich molecules, not fragments. Child typed/generic scaffold counts are 421/227, below Parent 560/380, with fragment-excluded mean initial similarity 0.235335 versus 0.264629. Numerous ring topologies exist, but the leaders remain related fused-carbonyl families with difficult-looking closures. Search sources (run-relative, Child copies are byte-identical to the frozen-request originals): policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-0/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-1/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0067-00-improve-L01/molecular/evidence/child/seed-2/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-1/trajectories/median_2.jsonl; nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-2/trajectories/median_2.jsonl.

There are 26 N-halogen-containing Child proposals, including highly scored N-F and N-Br substitutions. These should not be treated as conventional substituent optimization solely because the objective tolerates them.
No <=5-heavy-atom fragments occur in this Child task, unlike 11 in Parent; fragment loss is therefore not a universal remaining bottleneck.
missing_features: The lower-score proposals lack the leaders' combined substantial aza-aromatic framework and saturated nitrogen/carbonyl ring organization; neither a lone phenyl amide nor size alone captures this pattern.

The search does not show a broadly transferable scaffold solution: all seed leaders retain different related fused-carbonyl families, and the exact chemistry needed beyond the observed plateau is not identifiable.
Stereochemical specification and a demonstrated way to build the medium-sized/fused heterocycles are absent. Those are chemistry gaps, not established explanations for the remaining score.

The other seed leaders carry an aminooxy-containing indole/hydrazine-like system or a more densely fused fluorinated carbonyl framework. The digest cumulated-double-bond text rate is 0.0701. Imino, aminooxy, hydrazine-like and unsaturated O-containing rings create possible stability/tautomerism and synthesis concerns; no measured chemical failure is asserted.

A chemically coherent arrangement of carbonyl, imine and nitrogen functionality across diverse scaffolds is not established. Several top structures retain awkward cyclic imidate/enamine-like or N-N motifs, so no specific absent benchmark-answer motif can be inferred.
Defined stereochemistry and alkene geometry are absent in the fluorinated, partly saturated polycycles. Their effect on the supplied objective remains untested.

The leading Child combines moderate size, fluorination, nitrogen-rich rings and partial reduction: seed-best scores are 0.535627816841851, 0.48431891575512753 and 0.6452332956412979. transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-80d9b7174bc7 and its published code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, complete frozen Search panel at profile epoch 1, batch 10 and seeds 0/1/2. Accepted Child molecules include N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, an aryl hydroperoxide, terminal N-S substitution and dense heteroatom linkages; some occur among the highest observed scores. High-scoring Parent molecules also contain unusual bonds. This is an observed chemistry association, not attribution to the output-law component or a measured instability rate.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemical bond plausibility is not consistently maintained when editing otherwise substantial ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need chemically informed bond/valence-context handling that distinguishes ordinary amide, sulfonamide and N-O chemistry from reactive N-halogen, O-halogen or peroxide edits. Preserve access to useful heterocycles and ordinary amines; evaluate any such change through the same accepted-feedback contract rather than inserting objective-specific fragments or assuming a score benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source and conditions are the same complete n-80d9b7174bc7 Search panel versus n-cf8d309c06de. The pooled accepted streams contain both <=5-heavy-atom fragments with very low or floor scores and >50-heavy-atom elaborations. One Child stream contains no small fragments, so the gap is conditional rather than universal. Compact or moderately sized ring systems occur among the leaders, while greater size is not uniformly associated with better scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve a useful size and connected scaffold during structural variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Investigate task-agnostic graph moves that retain connected molecular context and can exchange or reorganize rings without involuntary fragmentation or repeated scaffold expansion. Use local accepted feedback to learn where growth or contraction helps; the descriptive size bins in this report must not become a hidden objective-specific template or an asserted universal optimum.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: all five frozen Child trajectory digests for n-80d9b7174bc7, 870 accepted optimizer rows per task across Search seeds 0/1/2, and the paired n-cf8d309c06de trajectories. Every Child digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit identifies possible tetrahedral centres in many substituted, fused and bridged products. The same absence of explicit stereochemistry occurs in Parent. This is a representation/chemistry omission; the visible scores do not establish that resolving it would help.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemical exploration and preservation are not demonstrated despite the generation of stereogenic ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A general generator could preserve existing stereochemistry and enumerate or vary valid local stereochemical alternatives when graph edits create stereocentres, while respecting canonical identity and the same oracle budget. Do not assert that a particular configuration or objective requires it without new authorized evidence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-80d9b7174bc7 versus n-cf8d309c06de under the complete matched frozen Search panel. Typed and generic scaffold counts increase in some accepted streams and decrease in others, while high-score molecules remain related ring-and-substituent families. Lower similarity to the supplied initial molecules sometimes accompanies more unusual bonding or poorer seed endpoints. These descriptors measure structural coverage, not a causal component effect or guaranteed useful diversity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffold novelty is not consistently coupled to preservation of coherent functional-group arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Test general scaffold transformations that retain ordinary local amide/amine/heteroaromatic environments while changing ring topology, instead of treating atom/bond novelty or scaffold count itself as a reward. Assess both typed and generic scaffolds, both size tails, and accepted-score outcomes with original source conditions retained; permit the task-local search to determine which arrangements matter.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
